# (PART\*) Getting started {-}

# Installation {#installation}

The package is installed directly from GitHub and works with R 4.0 or later.
Required dependencies, such as `sf`, `raster` and `terra`, are installed
automatically:

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("iep-ferreira/biomastats")
library(biomastats)
```

To update an earlier version, restart your R session and run the installation
again.

## Optional packages {-}

A few functions rely on packages that only their users need to install:

| Package | Needed for |
|:--|:--|
| `lconnect` | comparing `land_connectivity()` with the original `lconnect` |
| `future.apply` | `patch_imp_fast(parallel = TRUE)` |
| `osmextract` | `load_features(source = "osm")`, with regional OpenStreetMap extracts |
| `arrow` | `load_features(source = "overture")` |
| `ggiraph`, `htmlwidgets` | the interactive graph of `land_to_graph()` |

```{r eval=FALSE}
install.packages(c("lconnect", "future.apply", "osmextract", "arrow",
                   "ggiraph", "htmlwidgets"))
```

::: {.dica}
The package's plots are `ggplot2` objects. You can adjust them with extra
layers (`+ ggplot2::labs(...)`, `+ ggplot2::theme(...)`) and save them with
`ggplot2::ggsave()`. The analysis functions also take `language = "en"` for
English labels, as used throughout this edition.
:::
